title: Three Shades of Green
task: Find a single leaf, or a patch of leaves, that shows at least three different shades of green.
hint: Look at the underside, the veins, and the edges. New growth is often lighter.
learn: Leaf color changes with age, sunlight, and chlorophyll concentration.

title: Who Visited This Plant?
task: Look for a sign that an insect has been on a plant: a nibbled edge, a tiny hole, or a curled leaf.
hint: Check the lower leaves and the edges, where chewing damage is easiest to spot.
learn: Insects leave traces on plants long after they are gone, and these traces show who feeds on what.

title: Leaf Shape Showdown
task: Find two leaves with clearly different shapes and notice three differences between them.
hint: Compare the edges, the tip, and how the veins branch.
learn: Leaf shape affects how a plant catches light and sheds water.

title: Shadow Detective
task: Pick one tree and watch how sunlight and shadow change the look of its trunk and leaves.
hint: Look at the same spot from the sunny side and the shady side.
learn: Light and shade change color and texture, and plants grow differently on the bright and dim sides.

title: Nature's Geometry
task: Find a natural pattern that looks like a geometric shape, such as a spiral, hexagon, or star.
hint: Try flower centers, bark cracks, seed heads, and the way branches split.
learn: Many natural patterns repeat because they are efficient ways to pack, grow, or branch.

title: Texture Hunt
task: Find three different natural textures close to you, such as rough, smooth, and fuzzy, using only your eyes.
hint: Bark, stones, moss, and leaf surfaces all differ more than you would expect.
learn: Surface texture helps plants hold water, resist pests, or protect themselves from sun.
